transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Ethan Perez (Redwood AE), Zara Malik (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (CSM), Daniel Kim (CTO, Halcyon), Ruth Patel (SRE), Carlos Mendes (Eng Manager), Maya Torres (Product), Leo Park (Legal), Anika Bose (Ops)

Summary:
Quick tabletop style drill and customer-facing post-incident comms rehearsal following last week's production outage. Focus: what actually happened (short timeline), what we will commit to publicly, operational mitigations (canary, autoscale, rollback), and steps to rebuild confidence including credits/financial remediation and runbook changes.

Topics covered:
- Incident timeline and proximate cause hypothesis
- Root cause: driver-level GPU microreboots during rolling kernel update + hot worker re-initialization storm
- Immediate mitigations and rollback strategy
- Canary and autoscale tuning; admission control
- Customer comms draft and credit calculation
- Runbook updates and run drills cadence

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Perez: All right, thanks everyone for making time. we'll call this the credibility / comms drill, so the idea is run through what we are going to say and what we are going to do. I can start with a high-level 90-second timeline unless Zara you want to take the tech hit.
[00:18] Zara Malik: I can do it quick. so on 4/29 at ~01:27 UTC we saw elevated tail latency. the chain was: rolling kernel update -> a handful of NVIDIA driver microreboots on two racks -> immediate model process restart flood -> KV cache warmup storm and request queue pileup; multiple in-flight requests timed out which bubbled as 502s to customer. there's also an autoscaler race that exacerbated things, autoscaler spun up and down several times creating additional thrash.
[00:48] Daniel Kim (CTO): sorry, can you clarify the "microreboot" term? did the host actually reboot or driver reload?
[00:53] Zara Malik: good point — not full host reboots, it looks like the driver module did a soft-reset, so the GPU appeared temporarily unavailable to the process which triggered process-managed restarts. the model shards had to rehydrate from NFS and that was slow — we had a hotspot on weight loading.
[01:12] Ruth Patel (SRE): to add — our telemetry shows a ~45s window where token latencies doubled and queue length climbed. we hit the service-level backpressure threshold which should have tripped circuit-breakers but it looks like there were gaps in our admission control rules.
[01:28] Carlos Mendes: when you say admission control gaps, do you mean the thresholds were misconfigured or the checks weren't applied to the right path?
[01:33] Zara Malik: a little of both; some internal routes didn't run the same token-based admission filter, and the autoscaler reacted too aggressively because it was counting partial 'ready' responses as healthy which caused a restart loop.
[01:45] Ethan Perez: ok, step back. for the customer comms we need three things: a concise timeline, the root cause statement we can stand behind, and the remediation plan + what we will do to prevent recurrence. Priya, we want to rehearse the wording we will send.
[01:58] Priya Rao: agreed. I drafted two variants in the doc — one short for execs and one full postmortem. short version says: "We experienced an elevated error rate and latency due to a driver-level interruption during an infrastructure kernel update leading to model restart storms and queueing. We have applied immediate mitigations, rolled back the update in impacted regions, and are implementing further safeguards." Is that too technical?
[02:20] Daniel Kim (CTO): that's okay for our engineering leads; execs will want an even shorter blurb. also we need to decide whether to offer a service credit and how much. our contract mentions 99.9% but the outage impacted the peak hour; we need clarity on SLO exposure.
[02:36] Leo Park (Legal): on credits — we'll want exact minutes of degradation and the math used. we should also avoid language that admits product defect vs 'operational event' until both teams have finalized root cause.
[02:46] Ethan Perez: noted. we'll frame initial comms as "root cause under joint investigation" and be specific about mitigations already done.
[02:53] Samir Gupta (Support): quick note — we've had three high-severity tickets and multiple partners pinging about incomplete responses; we're planning to centralize the response.
[03:02] Zara Malik: mitigation recap — rollback kernel update in affected AZs (done), disabled aggressive autoscaler policy, added a driver-health probe hook to delay traffic routing until KV caches warm, and increased NFS parallelism for shard pulls. These are stopgaps.
[03:22] Carlos Mendes: can you walk through the probe hook? how will that avoid the warmup spike?
[03:27] Zara Malik: the probe will call into the model shim to confirm shard availability and KV cache fill for a short prefix. only when the probe passes will the node be marked ready. that prevents traffic from being routed immediately to a freshly spawned process that hasn't warmed.
[03:40] Ruth Patel: sounds good, but we should also add a randomized stagger to startup so not all workers warm at once — a jittered backoff.
[03:48] Zara Malik: yes, implementing exponential jitter on warmup sequence.
[03:52] [04:00] Daniel Kim: on long-term mitigations — what's the plan to avoid driver soft-resets causing this?
[04:05] Zara Malik: short term we have the probe and autoscaler lock. medium term: run rolling kernel updates with per-rack staged canaries and a conservative kill-switch if we see the microreboot pattern. longer term: validate driver/resident firmware across hardware and add better host-level isolation so process restarts don't cascade across the rack.
[04:25] Ethan Perez: for the canary plan, Zara, can you propose the exact metrics and thresholds? we need that in writing for Halcyon.
[04:32] Zara Malik: yes, I'll propose: maintain 95th percentile token latency within 1.2x baseline, no error rate increase >0.1% over 15m window, and no autoscaler flip-flop >2 restarts in 10m. failing metrics triggers rollback.
[04:50] Maya Torres (Product): will that add rollout time? I worry about delayed feature releases.
[04:55] Zara Malik: it will add a little more safety gating but we can do staged rollout by customer tenant to avoid global gating.
[05:03] Ethan Perez: good. next — comms tone and credits. Priya, read the exec blurb.
[05:08] Priya Rao: "On 2026-04-29 we observed elevated latency and intermittent errors affecting request routing during a routine infrastructure update. We have restored normal service and implemented immediate mitigations; a joint investigation is underway to confirm root cause and prevent recurrence. We will follow up with detailed timeline and remediation steps by May 6."
[05:28] Daniel Kim: I like that. for customers downstream we'll want a more technical appendix.
[05:32] Leo Park: also insert a line about compensation without admitting negligence: "We remain committed to rectifying any SLO impact and will propose a remediation package after the investigation."
[05:42] Samir Gupta: suggested credit proposal — prorated credit for the impacted window; we'll apply an automatic credit to the next bill and offer a 3-month priority help queue.
[05:52] Ethan Perez: ok, we will draft both the technical and exec comms; Priya will own the copy.
[06:00] [06:10] Carlos Mendes: ops question — the autoscaler logic that flipped, is that internal Redwood autoscaler or our override?
[06:15] Zara Malik: Redwood autoscaler with a tenant-level override we configured. the override unintentionally had lower cooldowns. we are changing default cooldown and adding a voter to consider node readiness probes before counting a node as healthy.
[06:30] Ruth Patel: can you share the log snippet where the restart storm aligns with the driver messages? we need to correlate to our observability windows.
[06:36] Zara Malik: yes I will include the raw logs and an annotated timeline in the timeline sheet.
[06:42] Ethan Perez: next — we want to rehearse customer Q&A: common ones we anticipate. Priya?
[06:47] Priya Rao: "Will this happen again?" answer: short — "We have rolled back the change, implemented immediate mitigations, and are adding a probe + canary process. A full joint postmortem will be delivered with concrete steps and timelines." Longer: technical countermeasures and driver validation plan.
[07:06] Daniel Kim: another Q — "Why did circuit breakers not stop the flood?"
[07:10] Zara Malik: answer — misconfig and path coverage gaps; we will deliver updated runbook and patch to apply admission checks uniformly.
[07:18] [07:30] Maya Torres: should we run a joint runbook rehearsal with Halcyon's on-call teams?
[07:35] Ethan Perez: yes — propose a joint drill next week. Priya you will coordinate.
[07:41] Priya Rao: noted. scheduling poll out by EOD.
[07:44] [08:00] Leo Park: legal — keep all comms factual, avoid speculative language about root cause until investigation wraps. also provide a mechanism for customers to request meeting with leadership if they want a private briefing.
[08:12] Ethan Perez: agreed. we'll finalize two templates: exec and technical appendix.
[08:20] Zara Malik: runbook changes I'm proposing: add driver-health as a first-class signal, gate autoscaler with node-ready vote, add jittered shard warmup, and add per-rack update rollback threshold. I'll open PRs to the infra repo.
[08:36] Carlos Mendes: what's the timeline for PRs and dry-run?
[08:40] Zara Malik: PRs in 48 hours, dry-run on staging within 96 hours.
[08:45] Ethan Perez: good — and we'll ask Halcyon to provide a staging window to run failover drills.
[08:51] Ruth Patel: we'll provide an anonymized traffic replay and a window for 5/9-5/10.
[08:58] [09:10] Samir Gupta: comms escalation plan: immediate customer email, scheduling the postmortem call, and a public status update. We'll draft and share by EOD tomorrow.
[09:22] Priya Rao: I will also create a short FAQ to accompany the email.
[09:28] Ethan Perez: last bit — reputational recovery. We should offer a transparent follow-up meeting with the customer's execs and a written remediation plan with milestones. do we want to offer a goodwill credit?
[09:40] Daniel Kim: yes, a credit is expected; amount TBD after your SLO math.
[09:44] Ethan Perez: action owners recap: Ethan send timeline and SLO impact spreadsheet; Zara share canary config and PRs; Priya draft comms and FAQ; Samir prepare credit calc and comms; Ruth share traffic replay window.
[09:58] [10:00] Carlos Mendes: one more notes on observability: we need to improve host-level fences in traces so we can quickly tell if the issue is driver vs model code.
[10:08] Zara Malik: adding an event tag in the trace for "driver-reset" and instrumenting firmware messages.
[10:12] Ethan Perez: ok thanks everyone. Priya will send the two comms templates later today and we'll reconvene next Tuesday to go over the postmortem draft.
[10:23] Daniel Kim: thanks, that sounds good. appreciate the quick response.
[10:27] [End of recording]

Notes & artifacts referenced:

Recorded sentiment / informal notes:

End of transcript.
